transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. It is most likely either a tripped thermal cut-out caused by restricted airflow or a failed heater element. However, before replacing parts, we must rule out simple causes. 1. Check the programme: Ensure you are not on a 'Cool Air', 'Refresh' or 'Delicates' setting, as these do not use heat. Switch to a standard Cottons or Synthetics cycle with the temperature set to normal/high.
2. Clean the lint filter: Remove the filter (usually inside the door frame) and wash off all fluff. If it was clogged, this restriction likely tripped the safety cut-out. Please try running a standard heated cycle for 10 minutes after doing these checks. Does the air become warm?
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check" — If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]
Did all that. Filter was fairly full so I've cleaned it, and I cleaned the vent hose out too, it was full of fluff. Still cold after 20 min on a normal heat cycle. Which part do I need?

[Heading: Failed heater element]
The two most likely causes are a failed heater element (which stops heating entirely) or a tripped thermal cut-out (a safety fuse that blows if airflow was restricted). To be certain which part to buy, I need you to check inside. Please switch off and unplug the machine. Remove the rear panel (usually secured by screws) and locate the heating assembly at the back of the drum housing. Look for a coiled wire element; if it is broken or has gaps in the coil, it needs replacing. If the coil looks intact but there is no heat, the thermal cut-out (a small sensor attached near the element) may have tripped. If you are not comfortable opening the machine, or if the element looks fine but still produces no heat after a reset, I would recommend calling an engineer to replace the heater assembly.

It's wedged against the wall in a tight alcove so I can't easily get round the back to take that panel off. I've also got no multimeter to test anything. It says DV7110 on the front, so can you tell me which part that likely needs?

[Heading: Failed heating component (element or thermal cut-out)]
Since you cannot access the rear panel to inspect or replace the heating element or thermal cut-out yourself, and you don't have a multimeter to verify which component has failed, this job requires an engineer. They will be able to move the dryer safely, remove the necessary panels, test the heating circuit for continuity, and replace whichever part is faulty (likely the heater element or the thermal cut-out). Please contact a qualified appliance repair technician.
